claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is an example of a single-phase bcc refractory high-entropy alloy under the stated operating conditions.
The initial random solid solution has high configurational entropy.
The initial refractory alloy has significant lattice distortion.
Intermediate-temperature annealing can nucleate and grow chemical short-range-order clusters in the single-phase bcc refractory alloy.
Rapid quenching preserves the topology of the annealing-induced SRO clusters.
Continued SRO development produces a transition from isolated clusters to a percolating cluster network.
The relevant transport regime occurs when the phonon mean free path is comparable to the SRO cluster size.
A suitable potential energy surface stabilizes specific atomic-pair correlations without causing phase separation.
Percolating SRO creates a continuous pathway whose phonon-scattering characteristics differ from those of the disordered matrix.
The percolating SRO network can act as a coherent channel or superlattice within the random solid solution.
Isolated SRO clusters produce Rayleigh-like scattering that lowers thermal conductivity.
Cluster coalescence at percolation reduces the density of highly scattering interfaces.
Phonons propagating through the connected ordered domains experience reduced Umklapp scattering.
Reduced interface and Umklapp scattering increases or stabilizes thermal conductivity after SRO percolation.
Deep local minima in the potential energy surface stabilize the percolating SRO topology against thermal fluctuations.
Thermal conductivity depends non-monotonically on annealing time or temperature, decreasing initially and then increasing or showing an inflection at percolation.
The post-percolation conductivity can approach or exceed the conductivity of the random solid solution.
Serial/parallel mixing models and random-alloy point-defect theories predict a monotonic conductivity reduction as SRO concentration increases.
The proposed percolative mechanism applies only while the SRO remains nanometer-scale and does not transform into intermetallic compounds or precipitates.
The mechanism fails when clusters are too small to percolate or when temperature is too high for SRO to persist.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as randomized at high temperature, yet the anneal intended to induce SRO is specified to occur above the randomization temperature. Without a different definition of that temperature, annealing above it should favor randomization rather than SRO growth.
